done_when: In a repo whose tests run in CI, where each merge to main runs main's own related tests, forge test --change and the one-group rule judge only the pull request's own changes (base...HEAD), so a small fix that merged main runs one group; repos that test on the laptop keep today's widening; new and existing repos get it on upgrade and forge sync

known.title: Merged CI changes can skip a failing integration test
Gate: merged CI pull requests run one group

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - a pull request and main edit different lines of the same module, while main also adds an integration test through an unchanged adapter.
The narrowed base excludes main’s new test, and the picker at src/forge/fasttest.py:433–448 matches tests only when they directly name the changed source. For example, a test importing checkout, which imports the changed pricing module, is skipped even if it fails on the combined tree; main’s green run tested the old pricing code. tests/test_merge_uses_ci_tests.py:118–150 demonstrates this selection failure, and a nonconflicting main edit to pricing makes the file sets overlap. The owner’s accepted mixing limit covers disjoint file sets, not this overlapping case (plans/FORGE-MERGEQ-1.md:23–25, 31–34).
Adds work: retain tests that exercise changed code through another module; F 2 x H 2 = 4; 2 x C = 4
findings.title: Merged CI changes can skip a failing integration test

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a small CI pull request has merged main and is eligible for the one-group shortcut.
The named proof checks only the classifier output. Its fixture uses a pytest command without an explicit {groups} count, so src/forge/prcheck.py:409–413 forces the generated workflow’s one-group output to false and the configured two groups still run. The test passes without checking that workflow decision. Use an eligible dynamically grouped command and verify the generated workflow’s resulting group count after the merge.
findings.title: Gate: merged CI pull requests run one group

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Gate
Case: normal use - a coordinator handles a pull request after main advances.
The new brief says CI selects only the pull request’s changes, but src/forge/templates/skill.md:363–364 still tells coordinators that CI selects tests added by the default branch. src/forge/story.py:88–95 ships that stale guidance to both agent hosts on sync, so coordinators are told that coverage exists when it no longer does. This breaks the standard: “Replacing behaviour deletes the old path, its tests and its docs in the same change.”
findings.title: Standard: Delete before adding

why: In repos whose tests run in CI, a pull request that merged main runs all test groups, because review-tests.py turns one_group off for any merge commit and forge test --change widens its base to what the merges brought; at a client almost every branch merges main, so small fixes take every fast slot (queue median about 16 min, up to 78)
